h1: Welding positioners — tilting turntables for round welds, 220 to 661 lb
intro: A welding positioner holds the part on a turntable and turns it under the torch at a steady, adjustable speed, so a round weld on a flange, pipe-to-plate joint, hub, tank head or wheel is laid in one continuous pass in the flat position — no stopping, repositioning and restarting around the part, and a more even bead whether the torch is held by hand or clamped in a holder. Tilting the table brings the joint to the best angle for the torch. NovoTech's premium-line WP 100 and WP 300 are built in Turkey: the WP 100 carries 220 lb on a Ø13-3/4″ table that tilts 120°, the WP 300 661 lb on a Ø18-7/8″ table that tilts 90°. Both turn 360° at 1 to 5.5 rpm, set on the control box and run from the standard foot pedal, with T-slots for clamps and fixtures, an optional 3-jaw lathe chuck and, on the WP 300, a custom fixture plate. They run on single-phase 220 V. Supplied and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: What does a welding positioner do?
faq.a: It turns the part under a stationary torch at a set speed, so a circumferential weld is made in one pass in the flat position — the easiest position to weld and the one that gives the most even bead. The welder no longer walks around the part or stops to reposition it; with the torch in a holder the travel speed is as steady as the table, which makes repeat parts faster and more uniform.

By the weight and size of the part. The WP 100 carries 220 lb on its Ø13-3/4″ table (110 lb with the table tilted) and tilts to 120°; the WP 300 carries 661 lb on a Ø18-7/8″ table (331 lb tilted) and tilts to 90°. The ratings are for a part centred on the table: a part whose centre of gravity sits off the table or far above it loads the drive more, so leave margin for long or overhanging parts.

faq.q: How fast should the table turn?
faq.a: Table speed (rpm) = travel speed ÷ (π × weld diameter). Across the WP's 1 – 5.5 rpm, a weld on Ø4″ pipe passes the torch at about 12.6 to 69 in/min and one on a Ø8″ flange at 25 to 138 in/min; set the speed on the control box for the process, wire and joint, and run the table from the foot pedal.

faq.q: What can be mounted on the turntable?
faq.a: The table is T-slotted (M10) for clamps, angle plates and fixtures. A 3-jaw lathe chuck of Ø6-1/4″ or Ø7-7/8″ (160 or 200 mm) holds pipe, shafts and round parts; the WP 300 also takes a custom perforated work plate for welding fixtures.
Single-phase 220 V — no three-phase supply is needed. The turntable motors are 0.33 HP (WP 100) and 0.5 HP (WP 300), and the foot pedal is standard.
